What's the coolest mathematical fact you know of?

The decimal fractions of seven are the same six recurring digits, in the same order, but starting from a different one each time.

1/7 = 0.142857142857...

2/7 = 0.285714285714...

3/7 = 0.428571428571...

4/7 = 0.571428571428...

5/7 = 0.714285714285...

6/7 = 0.857142857142...
On a related note, 142,857 happens to be my favorite number for this reason. You can do many cool things with it.
Care to elaborate? You have my attention.
Absolutely. I think this portion on Wikipedia about the number does a fine job of detailing the many neat tricks you can do.

Interestingly i notice there is no 3, 6, or 9 in that pattern. And there is A LOT you can do with those 3 numbers as well. For example:

3 = 3

3x2=6

6x2=12, 1+2=3

12x2=24, 2+4=6

24x2=48, 4+8=12, 1+2=3

48x2=96, 9+6=15, 1+5=6

Ect.

It will infinitely oscillate between 3 and 6. And if you add any of the answers to the answer before or after it, for example 48+96=144, the digits of the answer will add to 9. 1+4+4=9

There's something called a Schwarzschild radius. That basically is the the radius at which at a given mass would become a black hole. For instance if the Earth was compressed down into a sphere with a radius of a bit less than one centimeter, it would be a black hole. Now for the cool thing. The mass and radius of our visible universe match up perfectly with the Schwarzschild radius of a black hole.

This doesn't prove that our universe is a black hole, but I do think that it's a cool fact.
If the compressed Earth still had the same mass, then why would it's gravity be more?

Think about the equation for gravity:

  • G * m1 * m2 / r2

It's the masses of the objects multiplied by each other, along with a constant, divided by the radius squared. The radius squared part changes radically. The radius is measured from the center of mass of each object. That means fundamentally that it will be at least equivalent to the radius of the earth or about 6,300,000 meters. Now instead of dividing the product by 6,300,0002 we're dividing it by by 0.012 when you're right next to our blackhole earth. That's going to increase the force exerted by a factor of 400 thousand trillions (or 400 quadrillion)!

Basically you just make it where you can get much closer to the center of gravity. But if you stay the same distance, nothing would change. If our sun were a blackhole, the gravitational mechanics of the solar system would still work exactly the same.

These are exponential functions and they show up all the time in all the sciences and share the property that their rate of growth or decay is always proportional to the value of the function itself.
